A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GNP research, with matching architecture, training approach, theory and SuiteSparse benchmark. The text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 867 matrices, including convergence, timing, preconditioner failures and architecture/training ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional residual-ratio, application-area, timing and AMG-implementation analyses.

M1.justification: The scale-equivariant residual GNN, Arnoldi-based mixture sampling, residual training loss and nonlinear-preconditioned FGMRES procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 867 square, real, non-SPD SuiteSparse matrices using the same size and sparsity filters. v2 specifies 50 application areas instead of v1's 'over 20', without documenting added coverage. Structured-matrix applicability is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: Jacobi joins the direct GNP comparisons, alongside retained ILU, PyAMG, GMRES and unpreconditioned solves. Appendix D.3 additionally compares AmgX against PyAMG, although it does not provide a direct AmgX-versus-GNP solution-time comparison.

E3.justification: v1 uses a relative tolerance of 1e-8 and a 100-iteration limit throughout. v2 adds time-comparison runs with the iteration limit disabled and a shared timeout determined by the maximum solution time among the iteration-limited runs. This substantially changes the time-based evaluation budget; the AUC formulas and GNP training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds residual-advantage ratios, application-area breakdowns, construction-versus-solution cost analysis and a PyAMG–AmgX robustness study. The original sampling and scale-equivariance ablation questions remain. The convergence examples replace VDOL/kineticBatchReactor_5 with Hollinger/mark3jac040, including the corresponding appendix histories.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new residual-ratio percentiles and timing summaries describe variation across benchmark matrices rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 2 reports GNP's time-based winner share changing from 3.9% to 19.4%, and the unpreconditioned share from 49.6% to 3.7%, under revised stopping conditions and comparator membership; these are not same-setting performance gains. v2 adds residual-ratio results and AmgX failure counts of 105 during construction and 36 during solution. The retained failure table also changes GMRES solution failures from one to two.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, Corollary 2 and their original proofs are retained. New Appendix C derives an explicit Chebyshev-polynomial bound and approximately exponential residual decay under an origin-excluding spectral-ellipse assumption, extending the previously qualitative convergence discussion.

C1.justification: The four principal contributions remain. v2 narrows the first-work novelty claim to neural inverse approximation using only matrix information and newly claims applicability to structured matrices supporting fast matrix products. These refine the contribution's boundaries without redefining the proposed approach.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the practical interpretation: total cost depends on reuse across right-hand sides, generalization across different matrices is limited, and implementation choices affect robustness and speed. Appendix D.3 acknowledges that AmgX constructs preconditioners faster but fails more often, and explains why comparable solution-time testing is omitted. New discussion also connects GNN matrix products to polynomial approximation.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly discloses GPU use whenever supported and identifies the AmgX driver, configuration file and aggregation-based setup. It also explains the C-versus-Python implementation obstacle to solution-time comparison. Existing GNP hyperparameters and hardware specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The research positioning expands through connections to structured-matrix solvers, polynomial interpretations of GNNs, deeper GCNs, FCG-NO, AmgX and continual learning. Sections 1.2 and 5 develop substantive arguments about fixed sparsity and problem-specific generalization, while qualifying the novelty claim. This goes beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most method exposition remain intact. v2 makes targeted rewrites to the abstract, evaluation rationale and results discussion, reorders several results questions, moves Algorithm 1 into the appendix and organizes supplementary experiments into named subsections.

P2.justification: The result displays are substantially revised: construction-time plots expand to include solution times and additional methods, with logarithmic and linear versions; breakdown figures gain application-area panels; and convergence plots incorporate Jacobi and a replacement case. Two new tables present residual-ratio percentiles and AMG-implementation failures, and the existing failure table gains Jacobi.

improvement.justification: The revised time-budget protocol addresses an important weakness in v1, where early iteration-limited termination could favor fast but inaccurate solves in Time-AUC. Combined with construction-versus-solution analysis, application-specific evidence and the AMG implementation check, v2 offers substantially stronger support for assessing practical usefulness and its limits. Comparable AmgX solution-time testing remains unresolved, so the timing conclusions still depend on implementation choices.
